extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of New York / the ratifying public and policymakers considering the proposed Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Principled criteria for allocating taxation and revenue powers between a national government and constituent states, and for assessing the adequacy and effects of representative bodies for taxation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for future contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions of civil government must be framed upon a combination of existing exigencies and the probable exigencies of ages; there ought to be a CAPACITY to provide for future contingencies as they may happen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not limit national powers by present needs only; because future dangers (foreign war, domestic convulsions, loss of commerce) are unpredictable and potentially unlimited, the government should possess an indefinite capacious power to provide for emergencies. Anti-pattern: designing permanent provisions based only on temporary calculations of current revenue or needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design permanent provisions on permanent causes of expense
rubrics_metrics.description: In framing a government for posterity as well as ourselves, provisions designed to be permanent should calculate on permanent, not temporary, causes of expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning long-term revenue powers, base allocations on enduring obligations (e.g., national defense) rather than transient expenditures. Example: state civil lists vs. federal defense obligations; estimate state permanent needs low (~two hundred thousand pounds in the argument) while Union's needs are essentially unlimited.

rubrics_metrics.name: National responsibility for defense-related expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Wars and rebellions (support of national defense) are the chief sources of expense in every government and will dwarf ordinary civil expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate revenue authority at the federal level sufficient to meet large-scale defense and debt obligations. Illustration: in Britain fourteen-fifteenths of annual income went to war-related charges; similarly a republic must give the Union dominant capacity for defense spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exclusive assignment of large revenue sources to states
rubrics_metrics.description: Local governments ought not to command, in perpetuity, an EXCLUSIVE source of revenue for any sum beyond the extent of their permanent needs; extending such exclusive state power would divert resources from the Union that are needed for the public welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give states exclusive control over revenue sources whose scale exceeds their foreseeable needs; anti-pattern: assigning states exclusive claim to broad resources that are disproportionate to their fiscal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent jurisdiction in taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: A CONCURRENT JURISDICTION in the article of taxation was the only admissible substitute for an entire subordination of State authority to that of the Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent taxing authority reconciles an indefinite federal power with states' need for adequate independent revenue. It permits federal capacity without totally displacing state fiscal autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dangers of restricting federal taxation to particular objects
rubrics_metrics.description: If the jurisdiction of the national government in the article of revenue is restricted to particular objects, it would naturally occasion an undue proportion of the public burdens to fall upon those objects, causing oppression of particular industries and unequal distribution of taxes among states and citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of constitutional limits that confine federal revenue to narrow bases (e.g., imports only). Such limits invite distortive, excessive taxation on those objects, smuggling, monopolies, and inequitable state burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import duties are an inadequate sole funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties on imports should not be the only national fund because reliance on them alone would be attended with inequality and tempt the government to injuriously high duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement import duties with other resources (excises, direct/internal taxes) to avoid overburdening particular states, merchants, or consumers. Anti-patterns: monopolistic protection of manufacturers via exorbitant duties; increased smuggling; merchants bearing disproportionate tax when markets are oversupplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction and manageability of direct and indirect internal taxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal taxes subdivide into DIRECT and INDIRECT kinds; duties and excises (indirect) are often straightforward to assess and manage by reference to the article's nature or mercantile information, while direct taxes (e.g., land taxes) require execution by local assessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tax systems recognizing this distinction: use national legislative authority for principles and rely on local officers/assessors for valuations and execution. Example: adopt each State's existing systems within that state for collection and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: National legislature can and should use state administrative systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The national legislature can make use of the SYSTEM OF EACH STATE WITHIN THAT STATE; the method of laying and collecting taxes in each State can, in all its parts, be adopted and employed by the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid duplication and local ignorance, federal laws may delegate or adopt state mechanisms and officers for collection. This reduces expense, avoids double sets of officers, and mitigates friction between levels of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment by census and uniformity requirement as safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of direct taxes is to be determined by the numbers of each State (census), and 'all duties, imposts, and excises shall be UNIFORM throughout the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use census-based apportionment and uniformity clauses to limit partiality or oppression in federal taxation. These constitutional constraints act as checks on abusive taxation by the Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal taxing power strengthens requisition compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the federal government may forbear to exercise internal taxation, the existence of the power will give efficacy to requisitions by the Union, as States will be motivated to comply knowing the Union can act without them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain the constitutional power to tax at the federal level to provide leverage and fallback options, increasing the practical effectiveness of intergovernmental fiscal arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of local circumstances can be obtained by representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The national legislature can obtain necessary knowledge of local circumstances from the representatives of each State; those sent will generally possess the intelligence to communicate required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't assume lack of local knowledge undermines federal taxation; representatives and select enlightened statesmen can supply requisite information. Where minutiae are required, delegate execution to local officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution of taxation should be delegated to local officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The execution of tax administration, which requires local knowledge, must be devolved upon discreet persons in the character of commissioners or assessors, elected or appointed for the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation should set qualifications, numbers, appointment/election method, and general outlines of powers for assessors/commissioners, while leaving local details to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding double taxation in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The wants of the Union are to be supplied in one way or another; if provided by the federal government, it will not be done simultaneously by the State government — the aggregate burden need not be doubled by two governments levying the same tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design intergovernmental fiscal arrangements so that either level supplies the requisite revenue, reducing the risk of duplicated taxation. Use federal capacity (e.g., commercial imposts) to minimize recourse to more burdensome taxes that would affect poorer classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain emergency powers (including poll taxes) despite distaste
rubrics_metrics.description: Though poll taxes are disapproved, the power to have recourse to them ought to exist in the federal government because certain emergencies may make such expedients essential to the public weal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep constitutional flexibility to employ unpopular measures in grave emergencies, while recognizing and discouraging their routine use. Anti-pattern: eliminate emergency tools entirely — that can disarm the government when extraordinary responses are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of representation among certain classes will still represent broader interests
rubrics_metrics.description: From the natural operation of interests, whether representation be more or less numerous, the representative body will consist almost entirely of proprietors of land, merchants, and members of the learned professions, who will truly represent other interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess representative sufficiency by whether representatives (landholders, merchants, lawyers) can apprehend and promote general interests; practical voting behavior (mechanics voting for merchants) and the merits/skills required for deliberation make this composition acceptable. Anti-pattern: expecting literal one-to-one occupational representation without constitutional provision.
